plan.title: Walnut-Stained Console Table with Lower Shelf
plan.summary: A low rectangular display or console table inspired by the foreground piece in the photo: a solid top, four straight square legs, an apron frame, and a full lower shelf. The dimensions are estimated because none were provided.
assumptions: The foreground, lower table in the photo is the requested piece; the separate taller table behind it is not included.
Overall dimensions are estimated from the photo as a practical console/display table size.
Use poplar or another readily available paint-grade hardwood, stained walnut brown to match the pictured finish.
The top is a 25 mm solid-wood edge-glued panel; the lower shelf is a 20 mm solid-wood panel.
The table stands on a level floor. The square legs are kept straight for a practical build, rather than reproducing any subtle taper visible in the photo.
clarifying_questions: The photo shows a second, taller table behind the foreground table. Should a matching taller table also be included?

fasteners.name: Figure-eight tabletop fastener kit with screws

joints.drive_from: Before setting the base on P1, attach one leaf to the predrilled holes on the top face of each P2 leg; after positioning the base, drive the other leaf into the underside of P1 from below.
joints.note: One per leg. The swiveling figure-eight allows the solid top to move across its grain. Do not glue this joint.

joints.drive_from: From below, fit four clips into the inside-face groove in each P3 apron, then drive their screws upward into P1.
joints.note: Space four clips evenly along each apron. The clips permit seasonal movement of the solid top; do not glue or rigidly screw the top to the apron.

joints.drive_from: From below, fit two clips into the inside-face groove in each P4 apron, then drive their screws upward into P1.
joints.note: Space two clips along each side apron. Clips allow the solid top to move across its grain; do not glue this joint.

joints.drive_from: From the predrilled pocket holes on the inside face of each P4 apron into the broad face of P2.
joints.note: Glue and clamp the wood-to-wood contact. Use two 32 mm screws per leg connection; test the jig setting and screw length on scrap first. Screws enter the leg face, not its end grain.

fasteners.name: Slotted shelf angle-bracket kit with screws

joints.drive_from: From below and beside each corner, attach the bracket to the inside face of P2 and the underside of P5.
joints.note: One bracket at each shelf-to-leg contact. Use the bracket's slotted shelf-side hole, oriented to allow cross-grain movement, and use the screws supplied with the kit. These brackets supplement the shelf rails and are not the sole shelf support.

joints.drive_from: From the predrilled pocket holes on the inside face of each P7 rail into the broad face of P2.
joints.note: Glue and clamp each rail end to its leg. Use two 32 mm screws per contact; test the jig setting and screw length on scrap first. Screws enter leg faces, not end grain.

joints.drive_from: From the predrilled pocket holes at each end of P4 into the broad face of P3.
joints.note: Glue and clamp the apron corners square. Use two 32 mm screws per corner; test the jig setting and screw length on scrap first. Screws enter the face of P3 rather than relying on screws into end grain.

joints.drive_from: From below through the pre-cut elongated slots in the top face of each P6 rail into the underside of P5.
joints.note: Three screws per rail, evenly spaced. Cut and test-fit the slots before assembling the rails or placing P5. Orient slots across the shelf grain to permit movement; do not glue.

joints.drive_from: From below through the pre-cut elongated slots in the top face of each P7 rail into the underside of P5.
joints.note: Three screws per rail, evenly spaced. Cut and test-fit the slots before assembling the rails or placing P5. Orient slots across the shelf grain to permit movement; do not glue.

joints.drive_from: From the predrilled pocket holes in the ends of P7 into the broad face of P6, before attaching the rail rectangle to the legs.
joints.note: Glue and clamp the support-rail corners square. Use two 32 mm screws per corner; test the jig setting and screw length on scrap first. Screws enter the face of P6.

steps.title: Cut and label the parts
steps.text: Cut P1–P7 to the fixed dimensions in the plan, keeping each matching pair of rails and aprons equal in length. Label every piece with its part ID and position, and check the cut ends for square. Do not change the listed dimensions or placements.
tools_used: Miter saw or circular saw with straightedge
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection; secure stock before cutting and keep hands clear of the blade.
steps.tip: Check the saw setup on scrap first so matching parts finish at identical lengths.

steps.title: Sand and prepare the parts
steps.text: Sand exposed faces and edges of P1–P7 with 120 grit, then 180 grit; ease sharp edges lightly without rounding joinery surfaces. Test the walnut stain on an offcut and label the face of P1 that will be uppermost. Keep glue-contact areas clean and unfinished.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection; connect dust extraction or work in a well-ventilated area.
steps.tip: Sand with the grain on visible faces to reduce scratches that stain can make more obvious.

steps.title: Prepare holes, grooves, and shelf slots
steps.text: Set the pocket-hole jig for 18 mm stock and drill holes on the inside faces of P4 and P7 for their leg joints; also drill the end holes in P4 for J7 and in P7 for J10. Cut the Z-clip grooves along the inside top edges of P3 and P4, and predrill the figure-eight mounting holes in the tops of P2. Before assembly, cut and test-fit three elongated screw slots in the top face of each P6 and P7 rail, oriented across the shelf grain.
steps.safety: Clamp parts securely before drilling or routing; wear eye and hearing protection and keep the router base flat and moving.
steps.tip: Test the pocket-hole setup, Z-clip groove, and screw slots on scrap before preparing the parts.

steps.title: Dry-fit the lower support frame
steps.text: Arrange P6 and P7 into a rectangle at the lower shelf height, with the rail faces aligned and the ends seated. Check the diagonals and adjust until they match, then dry-fit the frame against the four P2 legs. Mark the shelf position without fastening it yet.
steps.tip: Equal diagonal measurements are a quick check that a rectangular frame is square.

steps.title: Assemble the shelf-support rectangle
steps.text: Glue each P6-to-P7 rail end and clamp the rectangle square. Drive two 32 mm coarse-thread pocket-hole screws at each corner from the end holes in P7 into the face of P6; first test the screw length and jig setting on scrap. Leave the clamps on for at least 30 minutes, or follow the glue label if it requires longer.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection when driving screws and keep fingers clear of the clamp jaws.
steps.tip: Wipe away squeeze-out before it dries, especially on faces that will be stained.

steps.title: Attach the lower rails to the legs
steps.text: Position the P6/P7 support rectangle on the four P2 legs at the plan's lower-rail height and clamp it in place. At each P2-to-P7 contact, apply glue and drive two 32 mm coarse-thread pocket-hole screws from the inside face of P7 into the broad face of the leg. Check that the legs remain square to the rail frame before the glue sets.
steps.safety: Support the frame on a stable work surface; get help if needed to control the legs and frame during assembly.
steps.tip: Use a square at each leg and compare the frame diagonals before tightening the final screws.

steps.title: Fit the side aprons
steps.text: Clamp each P4 side apron between its P2 legs in the upper apron position. Apply glue at each contact and drive two 32 mm coarse-thread pocket-hole screws per leg from the inside face of P4 into the leg face. Confirm the aprons are level and the leg frame is square.
steps.safety: Keep the partially assembled table supported so it cannot tip while you clamp and fasten the aprons.
steps.tip: Use a scrap spacer or marked gauge to keep both aprons at the same height.

steps.title: Complete the apron frame
steps.text: Place P3 between the side aprons and clamp each corner flush and square. Apply glue at the P3-to-P4 contacts, then drive two 32 mm coarse-thread pocket-hole screws at each corner from P4 into the broad face of P3. Leave the frame clamped for at least 30 minutes and recheck the diagonals.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while driving screws and keep the frame supported against rolling or tipping.
steps.tip: Do not force a corner into alignment with the screws; correct the clamp position first.

steps.title: Fit the lower shelf at the leg contacts
steps.text: Set P5 onto the lower support rails and center it in the opening, with its edges meeting the four P2 legs as planned. At each P2-to-P5 contact, install one slotted shelf angle-bracket using its supplied screws, with the slotted arm on the shelf side and oriented to allow cross-grain movement. Do not glue the shelf to the legs.
steps.safety: Support the table securely on its side or upside down while working underneath; use help if the frame is awkward to handle.
steps.tip: Check that P5 sits flat on all four rails before fastening any bracket.

steps.title: Secure the shelf to its support rails
steps.text: With the table securely supported and access to the rail undersides, drive three 16 mm pan-head screws through the pre-cut elongated slots in each P6 and P7 rail into the underside of P5. Do not add glue. The slots must remain loose enough to permit the solid shelf to move across its grain.
steps.safety: Keep the table stable while reaching underneath and wear eye protection when driving screws from below.
steps.tip: Do not overtighten the pan-head screws; the shelf must remain able to shift slightly in the slots.

steps.title: Attach the tabletop with movement-friendly fasteners
steps.text: Lay P1 face down on a clean padded surface. Before placing the base on P1, attach one leaf of a figure-eight kit to the predrilled top face of each P2 leg; then center the base and fasten the other leaves to the underside of P1. Install four Z-clips per P3 apron and two per P4 apron using the supplied screws, leaving each clip able to pivot or slide; do not glue the top.
steps.safety: Use a helper to lift and turn the tabletop and frame; protect the finished faces from the work surface.
steps.tip: Measure the overhang at all four sides before driving the final fasteners.

steps.title: Stain and apply the clear finish
steps.text: Remove dust, apply walnut-colored stain evenly, and wipe off excess according to the stain label. Let it dry fully, then apply the clear topcoat in thin coats, sanding lightly with 220 grit between coats when the label allows. Allow the final coat to dry and cure for the product's stated time before placing objects on the table.
steps.safety: Use stain and clear finish with strong ventilation, wear chemical-resistant gloves, and keep solvent-wet rags spread out to dry safely or dispose of them per the label.
steps.tip: Follow the finish label for recoat and cure times; a surface that feels dry may not yet be fully cured.

review.summary: The table is generally buildable, but the tabletop attachment at J1 needs redesign, and the two large solid-wood panels are specified as made from boards without a practical glue-up or sourcing plan.

issues.problem: J1 fastens figure-eight leaves to the end-grain top faces of the legs, which gives the screws poor holding power. The plan also does not provide the shallow recesses these fasteners normally need to sit flush, so they can hold P1 off the leg tops. J2 and J3 already provide movement-friendly tabletop attachment.
issues.fix: Remove J1 and its four fasteners, and rely on the Z-clips in J2 and J3 to attach P1. If extra attachment points are desired, use movement-friendly clips mounted to the leg sides and specify their recess and screw details.

issues.problem: P1 and P5 are specified as edge-glued panels but listed as parts to make from boards. The plan gives no edge-gluing, flattening, or panel-sourcing instructions, and these dimensions and thicknesses may not be available as standard poplar panels at a local home center.
issues.fix: Specify purchasable panels with a source and suitable finished dimensions, or add a panel glue-up method and the tools and stock needed to make and flatten both panels.

plan.title: Woodpecker Nesting Box
plan.summary: A wall-mounted wooden nesting box with a 50 mm entrance hole, deep enclosed cavity, overhanging flat roof, and raised floor with supporting cleats. Dimensions are estimated from the photo; the roof is kept flat for straightforward construction.
assumptions: Estimated overall size from the photograph: 240 mm wide, 239 mm deep, and 480 mm tall; the actual box is not dimensioned in the image.
Balanced-material choice: 19 mm exterior-grade pine boards, with a durable exterior finish. Actual board thickness is 19 mm.
The 200 × 200 mm body is centered under the wider roof; the back board extends above the body for mounting.
The entrance is a 50 mm diameter round opening, centered across the front and 275 mm above the box bottom.
The floor is raised 19 mm above the bottom edges and supported by two interior cleats; provide small drainage holes in the floor when building.
The photo shows a pitched roof; this beginner-friendlier geometry uses a flat overhanging roof instead.
Mount the extended back board securely to a tree using suitable outdoor-rated straps or fasteners; mounting hardware is not modeled as a wood part.
Leave the interior wood rough or add shallow climbing kerfs below the entrance. Confirm the entrance diameter and cavity dimensions suit the intended local woodpecker species.

joints.note: Use two long brackets spaced along the P1–P4 contact for substantial reinforcement. Put the slots on the P4 leaves and leave those screws just snug for floor movement. No glue.

joints.drive_from: After setting P6, drive the screws into the P6 top face from above and into the exterior face of P1 from behind.
joints.note: Use two exterior brackets for a stronger back-to-roof connection. Place the slots on the roof leaves, oriented across the roof grain, and do not clamp the slots or glue the roof.

joints.drive_from: Attach each bracket's floor leaf from below while P4 is outside the box in step 3; drive the remaining screws from inside the open box into each P2 face in step 4.
joints.note: Install one long bracket at each side-wall/floor contact. Put the slots on the P4 leaves and leave them just snug for floor movement. No glue.

joints.drive_from: After setting P6, drive four screws into the P6 top face from above and four into the exterior face of each P2.
joints.note: Use one bracket at each side-wall/roof contact. Put the slots on the roof leaves, oriented across the roof grain; leave the slots able to move and do not glue.

joints.drive_from: Attach the floor leaf from below while P4 is outside the box in step 3; drive the remaining screws from inside the open box into the face of P3 in step 4.
joints.note: Put the slots on the P4 leaf and leave those screws just snug for floor movement. No glue.

joints.drive_from: After setting P6, drive four screws into the roof top from above and four into the exterior face of P3 from the front.
joints.note: Fit the bracket below the roof overhang. Put the slots on the roof leaf, oriented across the roof grain; leave the slots able to move and do not glue.

joints.drive_from: From below P4, drive two screws into the underside of P4 and two into the face of each P5 cleat before placing the floor in the box.
joints.note: Use one bracket per cleat with a slot on the P4 leaf. Leave the slot just snug and do not glue across the solid-wood floor.

steps.title: Cut and prepare the boards
steps.text: Cut P1 through P6 to the listed dimensions without changing their sizes. Cut the 50 mm entrance in P3 at the specified position, and drill several small drainage holes through P4. Keep the inside faces rough for climbing, but ease sharp exterior edges with 80-grit paper.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection when cutting, and a dust mask when sanding. Clamp boards securely; keep hands clear of the blade and hole saw.
steps.tip: Mark the inside and outside faces before cutting so the rough climbing surface stays inside.

steps.title: Dry-fit, mark, and pre-drill
steps.text: Dry-fit the panels and mark the positions for all brackets. Drill pilot holes for the #8 x 16 mm screws, keeping the tips at least 3 mm inside visible faces; use a depth stop or tape on the bit. Mark the roof-bracket slots so they run across the roof grain, and check that every bracket will be reachable before the roof is attached.
steps.safety: Clamp pieces before drilling and wear eye protection. Keep the drill straight and use a depth stop to avoid breaking through a face.
steps.tip: Label each bracket location and its floor, wall, or roof leaf before taking the dry fit apart.

steps.title: Fit the floor cleats and floor-side brackets
steps.text: Place the two P5 cleats under P4 and fit one slotted 25 x 25 x 1 mm bracket at each P4–P5 contact. Fasten each bracket with four stainless #8 x 16 mm screws, two into each part; do not glue. Before bringing the floor into the box, attach the floor leaves of the P1, P2, and P3 brackets: use two 150 x 30 x 2 mm brackets at P1 and one at each P2 and P3 contact, with four #8 x 16 mm screws per floor leaf.
steps.safety: Support P4 flat on a bench while driving screws. Wear eye protection and keep fingers clear of the driver and bracket edges.
steps.tip: Keep all floor-leaf screws just snug in their slots so seasonal floor movement is not blocked.

steps.title: Secure the floor and reinforce the back
steps.text: Set P1, both P2 walls, and P3 around the cleated P4 floor, keeping the walls square. From inside the open box, fasten the remaining leaves of J1, J3, and J5 into the wall faces: use four #8 x 16 mm screws per bracket, including both P1 brackets, and do not glue these movement-friendly floor joints. Check alignment and tighten the screws without clamping the floor slots.
steps.safety: Brace the walls square or have a helper hold them while driving screws. Keep the top open and the driver path clear.
steps.tip: Confirm the body is square and the floor rests evenly on both P5 cleats before tightening.

steps.title: Fit and fasten the roof from outside
steps.text: Set P6 on the wall tops and align its overhangs before fastening. Fit two 50 x 50 x 3 mm brackets at the P1–P6 contact and one at each P2–P6 and P3–P6 contact; use four stainless #8 x 16 mm screws into each part for every bracket. Drive into the roof from above and into the exterior wall faces, leaving the roof slots free to move and using no glue.
steps.safety: Support the roof while positioning it and keep fingers clear of the edges. Clamp the box securely on the bench before driving the exterior brackets.
steps.tip: Check the side and front overhangs before fastening; roof-leaf slots must run across the roof grain.

steps.title: Sand and finish the exterior
steps.text: Lightly sand exposed exterior faces with 120-grit paper, leaving the interior and entrance climbing area unfinished. Apply exterior-rated finish to the outside only, following the product label for coats and drying; allow at least 24 hours or the label's longer stated time before handling. No glue is used at the slotted joints, so there is no glue clamp-up or cure step.
steps.safety: Use gloves and good ventilation when applying finish, and keep it away from flames. Follow the label's drying and disposal instructions.
steps.tip: Keep finish out of the cavity, drainage holes, and entrance; allow all fumes to dissipate before mounting.

steps.title: Mount the finished box
steps.text: After the finish is fully dry, mount the extended P1 back using a suitable outdoor-rated tree strap or mounting system installed according to its instructions. Keep the entrance unobstructed and orient the box for the target species and local conditions. Choose mounting hardware for the tree and expected exposure; it is not modeled in the fixed parts or contact list.
tools_used: Outdoor-rated tree strap or mounting system
steps.safety: Use a stable ladder only when necessary, have another person steady it, and do not overreach. Get help lifting and positioning the box at height.
steps.tip: Avoid fastening in a way that constricts the tree as it grows; check the mount periodically.

review.summary: The box is buildable, but the shell relies on slotted brackets for nearly all its connections, leaving it vulnerable to racking. The roof brackets are difficult to fasten after the roof is installed, and floor-movement slots need clearer orientation.

issues.problem: The wall corners have no specified direct connection. The shell depends on brackets connecting the walls to the floor and roof, and those joints are intentionally slotted and unglued. This leaves the box vulnerable to racking under wind and handling.
issues.fix: Add interior corner cleats at the vertical P1–P2 and P2–P3 seams. Glue and screw each cleat to the face of both adjoining walls, with pilot holes, before fitting the roof. Keep the floor and roof movement joints slotted as intended.

issues.problem: The P2-to-roof brackets are fastened to the exterior wall faces after P6 is installed. The roof overhang sits directly above these bracket leaves and can obstruct the drill/driver body, especially at the upper screws.
issues.fix: In step 4, fasten the vertical leaves of J4 to the outside faces of P2 before setting P6. In step 5, set the roof and drive only the accessible screws into its top face.

issues.problem: The J6 bracket is below the front roof overhang, but step 5 requires driving screws into the P3 face after the roof is installed. The overhang can prevent the driver from approaching the upper screws with adequate clearance.
issues.fix: Fasten the vertical leaf of J6 to P3 before installing P6. After setting the roof, drive the screws into the roof leaf from above.

issues.problem: P4 is wider than about 150 mm, but the plan does not specify the direction of the slots in the floor leaves. If those slots do not run across P4's grain, the surrounding bracket connections can restrain seasonal movement and split or distort the floor.
issues.fix: Orient the slots in every P4 leaf of J1, J3, J5, and J7 perpendicular to P4's grain, and leave the screws just snug rather than clamping the slots. State this explicitly in steps 2–4.

issues.problem: The mounting instructions allow a single tree strap, which may let the tall box rotate or wobble in wind.
issues.fix: Specify two vertically separated, outdoor-rated straps or an equivalent mounting system secured to P1. Install them without constricting the tree as it grows, and follow the mounting hardware's load and installation instructions.

plan.title: Painted Windsor-Style Armchair
plan.summary: A compact, sturdy wooden armchair inspired by the photograph, with a broad arched back rail, spindle back, shaped-looking armrests, splayed legs, and low stretchers. The seat is kept flat for a practical intermediate build; the curved back rail is cut from solid stock.
assumptions: The photograph is a close-up of a small wooden armchair; the complete dimensions are estimated at 620 mm wide × 600 mm deep × 850 mm high, with a 430 mm seat height.
Balanced materials: poplar solid wood for the frame and seat, with a glossy orange painted finish to match the image.
The sculpted appearance of the seat is approximated with a flat, thick seat panel; no carved saddle is specified.

The back rail is a custom-sawn arched profile. Use a bandsaw or jigsaw and sand the profile smooth; an off-the-shelf alternative is a straight Windsor chair crest rail, but it will not match the photo as closely.
Legs are straight square stock splayed outward in both width and depth; their ends are cut level to the floor. Back posts and spindles are hardwood dowels.
Aprons and stretchers are fitted between the legs with glued, screwed, or housed joints. Rail-to-leg and dowel-to-seat/back-rail joints are intentional structural joinery.
The photo is cropped and strongly color-shifted, so the chair proportions and presence of armrests are estimates.

joints.drive_from: From below through an elongated slot in each leg top into the seat underside, before fitting the apron clips.
joints.note: The seat bears on the leg tops; use one screw per leg through a 6 x 16 mm slot oriented across the seat grain. Do not glue the seat to the legs. The screw retains the seat while the slot permits seasonal movement; its 25 mm length leaves at least 7 mm beneath the visible seat face.

joints.drive_from: From below the seat, before turning the chair upright.
joints.note: Use two Z-clips at each front/rear apron contact. Fit them to allow movement across the seat grain; do not glue or rigidly screw the seat to the apron.

joints.drive_from: From below the seat, before turning the chair upright.
joints.note: Use two Z-clips at each side-apron contact. Orient their slots to allow movement across the seat grain; do not glue the seat to the aprons.

joints.drive_from: From the side of each support, driving two opposed screws downward into the seat face after seating the support in its hole.
joints.note: Fit each support into a 32 mm diameter, 28 mm deep blind socket, leaving at least 4 mm of seat above the hole. Glue the socket, then predrill and drive two #10 x 45 mm structural screws through the support base at opposing shallow downward angles into the seat face; keep the screw tips at least 3 mm from the seat underside. The deep socket and paired screws resist armrest leverage without relying on end-grain screws.

joints.drive_from: From the side of each back post, driving two opposed screws downward into the seat face after seating the post in its angled hole.
joints.note: Fit each post into a 32 mm diameter, 28 mm deep angled blind socket, leaving at least 4 mm of seat above the hole. Glue the socket, then predrill and drive two #10 x 45 mm structural screws through the post base at opposing shallow downward angles into the seat face; keep the screw tips at least 3 mm from the seat underside. joints.drive_from: From above the seat into the spindle holes, before fitting the crest rail.

joints.drive_from: From the pre-drilled pocket holes on the inside face of each apron end into the long-grain face of the leg.
joints.note: Use two pocket holes at each apron end. Apply a thin film of glue to the wood contact and drive two #8 x 32 mm screws per contact into the leg face, not its end grain.

joints.drive_from: From each stretcher tenon into its blind mortise in the leg inside face, as part of the complete frame glue-up.
joints.note: Cut centered tenons about 10 mm thick, 20 mm wide, and 20 mm long, with matching blind mortises in the legs. Dry-fit all four P5 tenons together with the P6 tenons and half-laps before applying glue; glue the tenon cheeks and mortise walls during the single complete frame glue-up.

joints.drive_from: From each side-stretcher tenon into its blind mortise in the leg inside face, as part of the complete frame glue-up.

joints.drive_from: At the exposed stretcher intersections during the complete P2/P5/P6 dry-fit and glue-up.
joints.note: Cut matching half-depth laps so the stretcher faces finish flush. Engage all four half-laps during the full dry-fit before glue is applied; pre-position clamps, then glue the laps and all four leg mortise-and-tenon joints in one coordinated assembly. steps.title: Make and flatten the seat panel
steps.text: Make P1 (solid chair seat) by edge-gluing several narrower poplar boards into one panel slightly oversize. Clamp the panel flat, let the glue cure for 24 hours, then flatten and trim it to the fixed 510 x 500 x 32 mm dimensions. Keep the grain running along the 510 mm length.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and a dust mask when planing or sanding; clamp the boards securely during glue-up.
steps.tip: Alternate the growth-ring direction of adjacent boards to help the panel stay flat.

steps.title: Shape parts and prepare the joinery
steps.text: Label the parts and mark the leg splay, apron pocket holes, stretcher mortises and tenons, and stretcher half-laps. Cut and sand the arched profile on P11; drill the seat sockets and spindle holes, armrest sockets, and cross-holes to their specified depths. Drill all pocket holes and screw pilot holes now, and prepare the leg-top slots for the seat screws.
steps.safety: Clamp parts before drilling, chiseling, or sawing. Wear eye and hearing protection and keep hands clear of blades and bits.
steps.tip: Test tenon fits and angled holes on scrap before drilling the finished seat or cutting the crest rail.

steps.title: Dry-fit the full frame and sand
steps.text: Dry-fit all four legs, both P5 stretchers, and both P6 stretchers together, engaging every mortise-and-tenon joint and half-lap at once. Check the frame for square, twist, and correct leg splay; also dry-fit the aprons and back components. Sand reachable surfaces through 120, 180, and 220 grit before assembly.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection while sanding, and use dust extraction when available.
steps.tip: Do not force a tight joint; adjust it before glue-up so the complete frame can close without being forced.

steps.title: Glue up the complete leg and stretcher frame
steps.text: Assemble P2 (legs), P5 (front and rear stretchers), and P6 (side stretchers) together in one glue-up, with all four half-laps engaged as well as all leg mortise-and-tenon joints. Pre-position clamps, then spread glue on the tenon cheeks, mortise walls, and half-lap faces and assemble the entire frame without forcing it. Clamp for at least 30 minutes, check square and splay, and leave undisturbed for 24 hours.
steps.safety: Use light mallet taps and keep fingers clear of closing joints and clamps.
steps.tip: Have all clamps ready before applying glue; the interlocking stretchers must be assembled together.

steps.title: Attach the front and rear aprons
steps.text: Attach P3 (front and rear seat aprons) to P2 (legs) at all four contacts. Apply a thin film of glue and drive two #8 x 32 mm pocket-hole screws at each contact from the inside face of the apron into the leg. Clamp for 30 minutes and allow the glue to cure for 24 hours before loading the joints.
steps.safety: Clamp the frame before driving screws and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Face the pocket holes inward so they remain accessible and hidden.

steps.title: Attach the side aprons
steps.text: Attach P4 (left and right seat aprons) to P2 (legs) at all four ends. Apply a thin film of glue and drive two #8 x 32 mm pocket-hole screws per contact from the inside face of each apron into the leg. Clamp the joints for 30 minutes and leave them undisturbed for 24 hours.
steps.safety: Keep the frame stable and wear eye protection while driving screws.
steps.tip: Check the apron tops are level with one another so the seat has even support.

steps.title: Attach the seat to the leg tops without locking its movement
steps.text: Set P1 (seat panel) on the leg frame and center it. At each P2 (leg) top, drive one #8 x 25 mm screw from below through the prepared 6 x 16 mm slot into the seat underside; orient each slot across the seat grain. Do not glue the seat to the legs or aprons.
steps.safety: Support the chair securely while working underneath it.
steps.tip: Tighten the screws just enough to retain the seat; do not clamp the slots so tightly that they cannot slide.

steps.title: Fit the seat-to-apron Z-clips
steps.text: Attach P1 (seat) to P3 (front and rear aprons) and P4 (side aprons) with two 25 mm steel Z-clips at each contact. Drive the clip screws from below, following the clip instructions, and leave the clips free to slide. Do not glue the seat to any apron.
steps.safety: Support the chair securely and keep the driver clear of fingers while working underneath it.
steps.tip: Check that every clip can slide in its slot and that no screw tip approaches the seat's top face.

steps.title: Install the front arm supports
steps.text: Attach P8 (front arm supports) to P1 (seat) in the two 32 mm diameter, 28 mm deep sockets. Apply glue in each socket and seat the support fully. Predrill from the support sides and drive two #10 x 45 mm structural screws at opposing shallow downward angles into the seat face; brace the supports until the glue sets and allow 24 hours to cure.
steps.safety: Clamp or brace the supports before drilling and driving screws; keep hands clear of the drill path.
steps.tip: Check the supports are plumb and at matching heights before the glue grabs.

steps.title: Install the rear back posts
steps.text: Attach P9 (angled rear back posts) to P1 (seat) in the two 32 mm diameter, 28 mm deep angled sockets. Glue each socket and match the planned rearward lean. Predrill from the post sides and drive two #10 x 45 mm structural screws at opposing shallow downward angles into the seat face; brace for 30 minutes and allow 24 hours to cure.
steps.safety: Brace the posts before drilling or driving screws, and use a helper if needed to steady the chair.
steps.tip: Use a straightedge across the post tops to keep them aligned while the glue sets.

steps.title: Install the back spindles
steps.text: Attach P10 (back spindles) to P1 (seat) at the three marked positions. Apply glue to the spindle ends, insert them into the 22 mm holes, and hold them at the matching back angle with a guide. Brace for 30 minutes and allow 24 hours to cure.
steps.tip: Measure the spindle gaps before the glue sets so the back looks balanced.

steps.title: Attach the armrests to the front supports
steps.text: Attach P7 (armrests) to P8 (front arm supports) in the 32 mm diameter, 30 mm deep holes in the undersides. Glue the sockets, then cross-drill through each armrest and support and fit one M6 x 90 mm through-bolt with washers and a locknut. Align the arms parallel and let the glue cure for 24 hours.
steps.safety: Support the armrests so they cannot fall or pinch fingers; clamp before cross-drilling.
steps.tip: Measure armrest spacing at the front and rear before tightening the locknuts.

steps.title: Secure the armrests to the rear posts
steps.text: Attach P7 (armrests) to P9 (rear back posts) with one 40 x 40 mm steel angle-bracket kit at each contact. Drive the supplied screws from below the armrest into the armrest underside and post side; do not add separate screws. Check that both arms are level before tightening.
steps.safety: Keep the chair stable and wear eye protection while driving screws.
steps.tip: Position brackets where they will not interfere with the user's hands or exposed edges.

steps.title: Fit the crest rail to the posts and spindles
steps.text: Attach P11 (arched crest rail) to P9 (rear back posts) and P10 (back spindles) using the prepared angled tenons and holes. Apply glue to the tenons and holes, lower the rail evenly onto all five parts, and clamp the back assembly for at least 30 minutes. Allow 24 hours to cure before moving or heavily handling the chair.
steps.safety: Use a helper to steady the chair and rail while positioning the arched part.
steps.tip: Center the crest rail side-to-side and seat all tenons together without forcing any one spindle.

steps.title: Install the anti-tip restraint where needed
steps.text: Fit one anti-tip strap between P11 (crest rail) and a wall stud if a child may pull or climb on the chair. Use the kit's 50 mm stud screw and supplied chair-side hardware, and verify the kit is rated for at least 200 N. Do not fasten the wall end to drywall alone.
steps.safety: Check for hidden wiring or plumbing before drilling into the wall.
steps.tip: The restraint is a precaution, not a substitute for supervision or correct chair use.

steps.title: Prime and paint the chair
steps.text: Sand away glue residue and ease sharp edges, then apply the interior primer and glossy orange paint according to the product labels. Apply thin coats and allow the labeled dry time between coats, typically about 4 hours; allow at least 24 hours after the final coat before careful handling. Wait 7 days, or the paint maker's stated full-cure time, before regular use.
steps.safety: Ventilate the room, wear gloves and a suitable mask, and keep finishes away from flames and ignition sources.
steps.tip: Keep paint out of the Z-clip slots and away from other moving seat attachments.

review.summary: The chair can be built with revisions, but the arm and back connections are too shallow for the loads they carry, the stretcher assembly order conflicts with the half-lap joints, and the side aprons have no connection to the leg frame.

issues.problem: The front arm supports are glued only 22 mm into 32 mm holes in the seat. With a 32 mm dowel, this shallow joint is not a reliable anchor for the leverage and side loads applied to an armrest. J11 uses the same shallow joint between each support and armrest.
issues.fix: Replace the short glued dowel sockets at both ends with substantially deeper structural joints. For example, use posts with long tapered or wedged tenons through the seat, and provide a deeper housed or through-tenon connection at the armrest. Keep the armrests supported by the rear posts as well.

issues.problem: Each back post is a round dowel glued only 22 mm into the seat. The posts carry the leverage from a person leaning against the back; this shallow socket is a weak primary connection. A small angle bracket at the armrest does not secure the post adequately to the seat.
issues.fix: Use back posts with long tapered or wedged tenons through the seat, or another substantial mechanical seat joint designed for chair-back leverage. Retain the post-to-crest-rail tenon connection, and do not rely on the armrest brackets to compensate for a weak seat joint.

issues.problem: The steps install the P5 stretcher frame in step 5 and the P6 stretcher frame in step 6, then call for cutting and gluing their half-laps in step 7. If the half-laps interlock as specified, the completed frames cannot simply be joined afterward without taking the leg joints apart or forcing the frame.
issues.fix: Dry-fit the complete P2/P5/P6 assembly with the half-laps engaged before gluing. Revise the glue-up sequence so the half-laps and all four leg mortise-and-tenon joints can be assembled together, with clamps positioned before glue is applied.

issues.problem: P4 side aprons have no specified joint to P2 legs. Step 10 only fastens them to P1 with sliding Z-clips, so they are not connected to the leg frame and cannot act as structural aprons or dependable seat-support rails.
issues.fix: Add a defined P4-to-P2 joint at both ends of each side apron and specify its hardware and assembly step. Keep the P4-to-P1 attachment movement-compatible; do not rigidly fasten the wide seat across its grain.

issues.problem: The 500 mm-wide solid seat is glued to all four leg tenons, while the glued stretcher frame ties those legs together. This rigidly restrains seasonal movement across the seat grain and risks splitting the seat or loosening its joints. The Z-clips at the aprons do not relieve restraint at the leg tenons.
issues.fix: Revise the seat-to-leg and frame design so the seat can move across its grain without being locked by the leg frame. Specify a movement-compatible seat attachment and ensure the apron and stretcher connections do not rigidly hold the across-grain seat dimension.

issues.problem: A 510 × 500 × 32 mm solid poplar board is not a normal home-center stock size. The plan calls it a solid panel but does not say how to obtain or make one; a single board that wide is unlikely to be readily available.
issues.fix: Specify an edge-glued seat panel made from narrower poplar boards, including the glue-up and flattening operation, or name a readily available panel stock suitable for the intended joints.

issues.fix: Update each joint's step field to the actual instruction number so the joinery and step lists can be cross-checked reliably.

plan.title: Rustic Outdoor Slatted Bench
plan.summary: A sturdy, two-person outdoor bench inspired by the photo, with a slatted seat and back, tall rear supports, structural side rails, and armrests connected to both legs. The photo has no reliable scale, so the dimensions are estimated for a typical garden bench.
assumptions: Estimated from the photo: 1500 mm wide, 595 mm deep, and 900 mm high; the seat is 449 mm high.
The photographed bench appears weathered and rustic. This plan uses exterior-rated cedar for the seat, back, and armrests, with pressure-treated pine for the structural frame.
The back is vertical and the armrests have squared ends; the photo's apparent curves and weathering are not reproduced.
The bench stands on a level surface. Use exterior-rated fasteners and finish appropriate for outdoor furniture.
P8 adds front-to-back side rails between the front legs and rear supports to brace each side frame. P7 armrests reach the rear supports and are mechanically connected there.
The lower back rail and seat are joined with slotted offset connector kits mounted underneath, leaving the surface behind the back slats unobstructed.

parts.name: Front legs
parts.notes: Vertical legs; their top ends support the armrests. Front seat rails and side rails meet their faces.

parts.name: Rear legs and back supports
parts.notes: Vertical supports; their bottoms rest on the floor and their tops set the overall bench height. They connect to the armrests, seat rails, side rails, and back rails.

parts.name: Seat support rails
parts.notes: Transverse rails. Their tops at y=430 directly support the seat slats; their ends meet the inner faces of the legs.

parts.name: Seat slats
parts.notes: Eight flat slats with 20 mm gaps, centered across the bench. Each rests on both seat support rails.

parts.name: Backrest support rails
parts.notes: Horizontal rails behind the back slats; ends meet the inner faces of the rear supports. The lower rail begins at the seat top.

parts.name: Vertical back slats
parts.notes: Nine vertical slats with 20 mm gaps. Their rear faces contact both backrest support rails, and their lower edges meet the seat.

parts.name: Armrests
parts.notes: Each armrest rests on the front leg and reaches the front face of the rear support. A structural angle connector fastens it to the rear support.

parts.name: Front-to-back side rails
parts.notes: One rail per side, tying each front leg to its rear support. The rails sit below the seat and are joined with pocket screws into the leg faces.

consumables.name: Exterior wood glue
consumables.note: Use at clean, tight structural wood-to-wood joints. Do not glue the movement-friendly seat connections.

consumables.name: Exterior penetrating oil or outdoor wood finish
consumables.note: Apply to exposed cedar and treated frame surfaces according to the product instructions.

consumables.name: Sandpaper
consumables.qty: A few sheets each of 80, 120, and 180 grit
consumables.note: Ease sharp edges and prepare exposed surfaces before finishing.

joints.drive_from: From the top end of P1 into the underside of P7, before the frame is assembled.
joints.note: Glue two dowels into accurately aligned holes, 25 mm deep in each part. This avoids relying on screws into P1 end grain.

fasteners.name: Stainless outdoor structural angle connector kit with supplied screws
fasteners.size: 50 x 50 mm, rated at least 1 kN per kit

joints.drive_from: From beneath P7 and from the front face of P2, before the seat frame is fitted.
joints.note: P7 reaches the z=525 front face of P2. Use one structural connector kit per armrest; its supplied screws fasten into the faces, not end grain.

joints.drive_from: From the pre-drilled pocket holes on the inside face of P3 into the face of P1.
joints.note: Glue the clean mating faces. Pocket screws enter the leg face, not the rail end grain.

joints.drive_from: From the pre-drilled pocket holes on the inside face of P3 into the face of P2.
joints.note: Glue the clean mating faces. Pocket screws enter the support face, not the rail end grain.

joints.drive_from: From the pre-drilled pocket holes at each end of P5 into the inside faces of P2.
joints.note: Glue each clean rail-end-to-support-face joint. The four contacts are the two rails at the two rear supports.

joints.drive_from: From the top face of each P4 slat down through a slotted hole in P3.
joints.note: No glue. Orient the slots across the bench width to allow cedar movement; one screw is centered at each of the 16 rail-to-slat contacts.

fasteners.name: Stainless slotted offset seat-to-back connector kit with supplied screws
fasteners.size: 19 mm offset, rated at least 1 kN per kit

joints.drive_from: From below, attaching the slotted kit between the underside of P4 and the underside of the lower P5 rail.
joints.note: Use one 19 mm offset kit at each contact. The offset bridges the 19 mm difference in underside levels; its slot runs across the bench for seasonal movement. It does not occupy the front face where P6 must sit.

joints.drive_from: From the front face of P6 into the face of P5, while the rail faces remain clear.
joints.note: No glue. Two screws per contact hold each slat to each rail; the 45 mm screws pass through P6 and enter P5 by about 26 mm.

fasteners.name: Stainless outdoor angle bracket kit with supplied screws
fasteners.size: 25 x 25 mm, supplied #8 x 12 mm screws

joints.drive_from: From below P4 and from the forward-facing face of P6 at z=506.
joints.note: Use one kit per listed contact, with one leg beneath P4 and the other on the exposed front face of P6 below the seat. No glue. The bracket and screws stay clear of the P5-to-P6 bearing face.

joints.drive_from: From the inside-facing pocket holes near the front end of P8 into the face of P1.
joints.note: Glue the clean mating faces. The two contacts are the front ends of the two side rails.

joints.drive_from: From the inside-facing pocket holes near the rear end of P8 into the face of P2.
joints.note: Glue the clean mating faces. Together with J10, these side rails brace the front legs to the rear supports without relying on the seat slats.

fasteners.name: Outdoor anti-tip restraint kit with stud screws
fasteners.size: Rated at least 450 N per strap

joints.drive_from: From the rear face of each P2 into a wall stud, after locating the studs.
joints.note: Use two restraints, each secured to a stud and rated for at least 450 N (100 lbf). Do not rely on drywall alone; use a separately load-rated masonry fixing if there are no wood studs.

steps.title: Cut the parts to size
steps.text: Cut P1–P8 to the listed lengths, using a stop block for matching pairs and repeated slats. Check every cut against the part dimensions before moving on.
tools_used: 305 mm (12-inch) miter saw with at least 90 mm cutting capacity
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection. Keep hands clear of the blade, support long stock, and wait for the blade to stop before lifting it.
steps.tip: A circular saw with a square guide or a handsaw and miter box can substitute, but verify square cuts and the full 70 mm leg thickness.

steps.title: Check the parts and dry-fit the frame
steps.text: Confirm the parts are straight, dry, and free of loose knots at the joints. Lay out P1 (front legs), P2 (rear supports), P3 (seat rails), P5 (back rails), P7 (armrests), and P8 (side rails) in their planned positions and check the contact faces fit flush.
steps.tip: Pressure-treated lumber must be dry enough for exterior glue to bond; follow the glue maker's moisture guidance.

steps.title: Pre-sand the exposed surfaces
steps.text: Sand edges and broad faces with 80 grit, then 120 grit; use 180 grit on cedar touch surfaces. Ease sharp edges slightly without changing the fixed part dimensions.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and a suitable dust mask; collect pressure-treated sawdust and dispose of it safely.
steps.tip: Sand mating faces before assembly, but keep glue areas clean and free of finish.

steps.title: Drill the joinery holes and slots
steps.text: Drill aligned 10 mm dowel holes 25 mm deep for P1-to-P7, pocket holes at each P3, P5, and P8 rail end, and the threaded-insert pilot holes in the lower P5 rail. Make the P3 screw slots and the P4 slots for the offset connector kits before assembly; test all depths on offcuts.
steps.safety: Clamp each part before drilling or slotting, wear eye protection, and keep hands clear of bits and blades.
steps.tip: Label mating faces before drilling. Orient the seat connector slots across the bench width for wood movement.

steps.title: Join the armrests to the side supports
steps.text: Attach each P7 (armrest) to P1 (front leg) with two 10 x 50 mm dowels, using exterior glue in the holes and clamping square for at least 60 minutes. Connect the rear end of each P7 to P2 (rear support) with one 50 x 50 mm structural angle connector kit and its supplied screws; allow the glued dowels to cure 24 hours before loading.
steps.safety: Clamp pieces securely and wear eye protection while driving connector screws; follow the glue label for skin protection.
steps.tip: Keep P1 and P2 parallel and confirm P7 reaches the P2 face before driving the connector screws.

steps.title: Attach the back rails
steps.text: Attach P5 (backrest support rails) to P2 at all four contacts using two #10 x 76 mm exterior structural pocket screws per contact, driven from the rail-end pockets into the support faces. Apply exterior glue to clean mating faces, clamp the rails flush, and keep the pocket openings clear while driving.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep the driver aligned with each pocket to prevent bit slip.
steps.tip: Check both rails for parallel alignment before tightening the screws.

steps.title: Build the seat and side frames
steps.text: Attach P3 (seat support rails) to P1 and P2 using two #10 x 76 mm pocket screws per contact, driven from P3's inside-face pockets into the leg faces. Attach each P8 (side rail) between P1 and P2 with two #10 x 76 mm pocket screws at each end; glue every clean structural mating face and clamp the frame square while tightening.
steps.safety: This assembly is awkward to handle; get help supporting it and keep the work on a stable bench.
steps.tip: Measure diagonally across the frame in both directions; matching measurements indicate it is square.

steps.title: Fasten the seat slats
steps.text: Space the eight P4 (seat slats) with 20 mm gaps and center them on P3. At each of the 16 contacts, drive one stainless #8 x 45 mm screw through the slat and its slotted hole into P3; use no glue so the cedar can move seasonally.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep fingers clear of screw locations.
steps.tip: Pilot-drill the cedar and center screws in the slots; do not overtighten and clamp the slat rigidly.

steps.title: Connect the seat to the lower back rail
steps.text: Install one 19 mm offset slotted seat-to-back connector kit at each of the eight P4-to-P5 contacts. From below, fasten each kit between the underside of P4 and the underside of the lower P5 rail using only the kit's supplied screws; do not glue this movement-friendly connection.
steps.safety: Support the bench securely while working underneath it; do not reach under an unstable frame.
steps.tip: Center the slots across the bench width and confirm the offset connector does not protrude into the P6 bearing face.

steps.title: Attach the vertical back slats
steps.text: Position the nine P6 (vertical back slats) against both P5 rails with the planned 20 mm gaps. At each of the 18 contacts, drive two stainless #8 x 45 mm screws from the front face of P6 into P5; use no glue and keep the screw tips inside the far faces of the rails.
steps.safety: Support the slats so they cannot fall while fastening, and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Pilot-drill the cedar and keep both screws centered on the rail face to prevent splitting.

steps.title: Fasten the seat-to-back corner brackets
steps.text: At the 14 listed P4-to-P6 contacts, fit one 25 x 25 mm stainless outdoor angle-bracket kit per contact. Fasten one leg beneath P4 and the other to the exposed forward-facing face of P6 below the seat, using the kit's supplied #8 x 12 mm screws and no glue.
steps.safety: Keep the bench supported and stable while reaching beneath the seat; wear eye protection while driving screws.
steps.tip: Check that each bracket is on the front face of P6, not the rear face against P5, so the slats remain seated flush.

steps.title: Apply the outdoor finish
steps.text: Brush exterior penetrating oil or outdoor finish onto all accessible surfaces, following the product's coverage and ventilation directions. Allow at least 24 hours between coats or until the label says it is dry, and wait at least 72 hours after the final coat before normal use.
steps.safety: Work outdoors or with strong ventilation; wear the finish maker's recommended gloves and respirator. Safely store or dispose of oil-soaked rags because they can self-heat.
steps.tip: Coat end grain and the undersides of slats as well as visible faces, without leaving pooled finish.

steps.title: Install anti-tip restraints if wall-adjacent
steps.text: For a bench placed beside a house wall, fit two outdoor anti-tip restraint kits from the rear of P2 to wall studs. Use the supplied stud screws and verify each strap is rated for at least 450 N (100 lbf); do not fasten into drywall alone.
steps.safety: Use a stable platform if reaching above shoulder height, and have another adult steady it.
steps.tip: For masonry, use a separately load-rated masonry fixing rather than an unverified plastic plug.

safety_overview: Wear eye and hearing protection for cutting and drilling; use a dust mask when sanding, especially around pressure-treated lumber.
Clamp work before drilling or slotting, keep hands clear of blades and bits, and pilot-drill hardwoods and holes within 25 mm of an end.
Use exterior-rated fasteners and follow glue and finish labels for ventilation, skin protection, curing, and disposal.
Get help moving the assembled bench; keep it supported when working underneath or fastening the back slats.
If installing wall restraints, locate studs and use the specified rated hardware; never rely on drywall alone.

review.summary: The bench is buildable in principle, but the side frame is inadequately tied together and the seat/back bracket instructions conflict with the assembled parts. Clarify the armrest connections, revise the bracket detail, and add the omitted cutting operation before issuing the plan.

issues.problem: There are no side aprons or stretchers connecting each front leg P1 to its rear support P2. The frame relies on the seat slats and their screws to tie the front and rear legs together, making the side frames vulnerable to racking under use.
issues.fix: Add a structural front-to-back side rail on each side between P1 and P2, with a specified load-appropriate mechanical connection, and install it before the seat slats. Do not rely on the cedar seat slats as the only side-frame brace.

issues.problem: J8 calls for brackets on the back face of P6 at the seat, but the lower P5 rail occupies that area behind the slats. The bracket leg cannot be fastened there as described; brackets installed on the front of P5 in step 8 also occupy the surface where P6 must sit flush.
issues.fix: Redesign the seat-to-back connection so its fasteners are accessible and do not obstruct P6 seating against P5. Show the revised bracket or connector locations and install any hardware that would be covered before fitting the back slats.

issues.problem: Step 4 and joints J1/J3 attach each armrest only to a front leg. No joint connects the armrest to the rear support, despite the plan describing that contact. The armrest therefore does not tie the side frame together or provide the stated rear support.
issues.fix: Specify a P7-to-P2 connection and ensure the armrest physically reaches P2. Give the joint and fasteners, and add the connection step before the rear/seat assembly makes the joint difficult to access.

issues.problem: All parts are listed as stock to be made, but no step or listed tool cuts the boards to the specified lengths. The parts are not all ordinary pre-cut sizes, so a builder cannot follow the plan using the stated tool list alone.
issues.fix: Add a cut-to-size step and list a suitable saw and setup, or explicitly identify which parts can be ordered pre-cut to the stated dimensions.

issues.problem: J1 and J3 describe the same two P1-to-P7 connections, but step 4 describes only two dowels per leg, while the duplicated joint entries and hardware list specify eight dowels total.
issues.fix: Remove the duplicate joint entry or reconcile the joint counts, step text, and dowel quantity so they all specify the same installation.

plan.title: Two-Step Wooden Step Stool
plan.summary: A compact two-step stool with dark plywood side cheeks, two hardwood treads, and supporting cleats. Sized as a practical estimate from the photo; all parts fit within the stated overall dimensions.
assumptions: The photo shows a freestanding two-step stool; dimensions are estimated because no target dimensions or scale reference were provided.
Overall dimensions are 460 mm wide × 475 mm deep × 400 mm high. The front is z=0.
Use 18 mm birch plywood for the two shaped side cheeks and hardwood for the 25 mm treads and 18 mm cleats; stain the cheeks dark and the treads a warm brown to match the photo.
The side-cheek profile is a stepped solid outline. Treads are supported by cleats fixed to the inner faces of the cheeks; use glued and screwed joints, with screw locations predrilled.
Treads are plain rounded rectangles with a small 8 mm plan-view corner radius. Ease exposed top edges lightly after assembly.
The stool is intended for one adult standing on one tread at a time; place on a level floor and do not use as a ladder.

parts.name: Stepped side cheek
parts.notes: Profile coordinates use u along depth z (0–475) and v along height y (0–345). The two identical cheeks occupy the outer 18 mm of the stool width.

parts.name: Lower tread
parts.material: 25 mm solid hardwood, such as poplar or oak
parts.notes: Rests on the lower pair of cleats. Its top is at y=203 mm.

parts.name: Upper tread
parts.material: 25 mm solid hardwood, such as poplar or oak
parts.notes: Rests on the upper pair of cleats. Its top is at y=400 mm.

parts.name: Lower tread support cleat
parts.notes: Each cleat is fixed to the inner face of a side cheek. Its top face at y=178 touches the lower tread underside.

parts.name: Upper tread support cleat
parts.notes: Each cleat is fixed to the inner face of a side cheek. Its top face at y=375 touches the upper tread underside.

consumables.name: Wood glue
consumables.note: For cleats and tread-to-cleat joints.

consumables.name: Wood screws
consumables.note: Use suitable predrilled screws to fasten cleats to the plywood cheeks and treads to cleats; screws are not included as parts.

consumables.name: Dark wood stain
consumables.note: For the plywood side cheeks.

consumables.name: Hardwood stain or finish
consumables.note: Warm brown finish for the treads; apply a compatible clear coat if desired.

consumables.name: Sandpaper
consumables.note: For shaping, smoothing, and finish preparation.

joints.drive_from: No fastener; bring P2 into position between the inner faces of P1 while the cheeks are upright.
joints.note: Intentional bearing contact only: each tread end abuts a cheek, but is not glued or screwed to it. P2 is secured by the cleats; this avoids relying on screws into tread end grain.

fasteners.name: Steel angle-bracket kit with supplied screws

joints.drive_from: From the inside face of P1 and the exposed side of P4, before either tread is installed.
joints.note: Use two brackets per cleat, spaced near its ends. Apply wood glue to the mating wood faces and install the bracket-kit screws into the predrilled holes; the kit includes its screws.

fasteners.name: Steel angle-bracket kit with supplied screws

joints.drive_from: From the inside face of P1 and the exposed side of P5, before either tread is installed.
joints.note: Use two brackets per cleat, spaced near its ends. Apply wood glue to the mating wood faces and install the bracket-kit screws into the predrilled holes; the kit includes its screws.

joints.drive_from: From below, upward through the predrilled cleat holes, before P3 is attached.
joints.note: Use three screws per cleat, one through the centered round hole and two through slots elongated along the tread depth. Use washers and snug screws without crushing the wood; do not glue, so P2 can move across its grain.

joints.drive_from: From below, upward through the predrilled cleat holes, before final finishing.
joints.note: Use three screws per cleat, one through the centered round hole and two through slots elongated along the tread depth. Use washers and snug screws without crushing the wood; do not glue, so P3 can move across its grain.

steps.title: Lay out and cut the side cheeks
steps.text: Mark the stepped profile on both P1 (Stepped side cheek) blanks, checking that the two profiles are mirror-matched for assembly. Cut just outside the lines with a jigsaw, then sand to the lines and verify the pair together.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection and a dust mask. Clamp the plywood securely, keep hands clear of the blade, and support the offcut so it cannot pinch the saw.
steps.tip: Mark the inside faces before cutting so you do not accidentally make two cheeks facing the same way.

steps.title: Cut treads and cleats
steps.text: Cut P2 (Lower tread) to 424 × 235 × 25 mm and P3 (Upper tread) to 424 × 215 × 25 mm. Cut two P4 cleats to 235 mm and two P5 cleats to 215 mm, keeping each at its specified 18 × 30 mm section. Round the tread plan corners to an 8 mm radius and ease only the exposed top edges.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection and a dust mask. Clamp stock before cutting; keep hands away from the blade and support long pieces.
steps.tip: Label each cleat by tread and side as soon as it is cut; the lower and upper cleats are different lengths.

steps.title: Sand and prepare the screw holes
steps.text: Sand the parts progressively with 80, 120, then 180 grit, removing sharp splinters but preserving the cheek profiles. In each cleat, mark three screw positions along its length: one centered and two about 45 mm from the ends. Drill the outer holes as short slots aligned along the cleat length, and drill bracket pilot holes using the bracket kit as a template.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection while sanding and drilling. Clamp small parts before drilling; keep loose clothing and hair clear of rotating tools.
steps.tip: The slots must run along the tread depth, not across the stool width, to allow the solid treads to move across their grain.

steps.title: Apply the finishes before assembly
steps.text: Apply dark stain to P1 and warm-brown stain or finish to P2 and P3, following the product label. Keep the cleat glue-contact areas on P1 bare, and keep the cleat contact faces bare; remove masking only when the finish is fully dry. Allow at least 24 hours or the manufacturer's longer stated drying time before assembly; the finish will need its full cure time before anti-slip strips are applied.
steps.safety: Work with ventilation, wear finish-appropriate gloves, and keep stain-soaked rags spread flat outdoors to dry or dispose of them as directed; they can self-heat and ignite.
steps.tip: Do not get stain or finish on glue surfaces; a clean, bare mating surface gives a more dependable glue bond.

steps.title: Dry-fit the cheek and cleat positions
steps.text: Lay P1 (Stepped side cheek) inner-face up on a protected flat surface. Place P4 (Lower tread support cleat) and P5 (Upper tread support cleat) at their marked step levels and check that the tread-support faces are level and the two cheek layouts mirror each other. Make pencil marks for bracket locations, then remove the cleats.
steps.tip: Confirm the lower and upper cleats are at the stated levels before drilling or gluing; a small height mismatch makes the stool rock.

steps.title: Attach the lower cleats
steps.text: Apply a thin, even coat of wood glue to each P1–P4 mating face and position both P4 cleats on the inner faces of the two cheeks. Fit two 30 × 30 × 2 mm angle brackets per cleat, using the screws supplied with the bracket kit and its predrilled holes. Clamp or hold each assembly square for 30 minutes, then leave the glue to cure for 24 hours before loading it.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while driving screws and wipe glue with a damp cloth. Support the cheeks securely so they cannot tip while you work.
steps.tip: Check that the two lower cleats are level with each other before the glue sets.

steps.title: Attach the upper cleats
steps.text: Apply wood glue to each P1–P5 mating face and position the two P5 cleats at the upper tread level. Install two 30 × 30 × 2 mm angle brackets per cleat with the supplied kit screws, then check alignment with a square. Clamp or hold for 30 minutes and let the glue cure for 24 hours before adding the treads.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while driving screws. Keep the assembly supported and stable, and wipe away glue before it hardens.
steps.tip: The upper cleats must be parallel to the lower cleats and flush to their marked step positions.

steps.title: Install the lower tread
steps.text: Set P2 (Lower tread) onto the two P4 cleats, with its ends just abutting the inner faces of P1; do not glue or screw the tread ends to the cheeks. From below, install three 45 mm #8 pan-head screws and washers through each cleat: one centered and two through the depth-aligned slots. Tighten only until secure, leaving the slotted positions free to move slightly; the 45 mm screws penetrate about 15 mm into the tread.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep the stool supported so it cannot shift while you drive screws from underneath.
steps.tip: Do not overtighten the slotted screws or add glue under the solid tread; either can restrict seasonal wood movement.

steps.title: Install the upper tread
steps.text: Set P3 (Upper tread) onto the two P5 cleats, with its ends just abutting the inner faces of P1 and no glue at the ends. From below, install three 45 mm #8 pan-head screws and washers through each cleat: one centered and two through the depth-aligned slots. Tighten gently so the tread is held down while the slotted connections can still accommodate wood movement.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and support the stool securely while driving the screws from below.
steps.tip: Check that each tread sits fully on both cleats before fastening; do not use the screws to pull a misaligned tread into place.

steps.title: Inspect, add anti-slip strips, and allow the finish to cure
steps.text: Check that all brackets are secure, the treads sit flat, and no screw tips have reached a visible surface. Once the tread finish has fully cured—not just dried—apply durable, adhesive-backed anti-slip strips intended for stair steps to the top of both P2 and P3; follow the strip maker's surface-preparation and application directions. Let the strips bond for the specified time before use, then place the stool on a level floor and use only one step at a time; it is not a ladder.
steps.safety: Wear gloves and ventilate while touching up finish. Do not use the stool until the finish is fully cured and both anti-slip strips are firmly bonded; have a second person help if needed when moving the assembled stool.
steps.tip: Clean the tread tops as directed by the strip manufacturer and keep the strips clear of rounded edges. A small amount of tread movement across the slots is intentional; do not tighten those screws until the slots are locked.

plan.title: Round Side Table
plan.summary: A 600 mm round side table with a 25 mm plywood top, four outward-splayed tapered legs, and a centered underside cleat, matching the drawing.
assumptions: The supplied target dimensions govern: the top is 600 mm in diameter and 25 mm thick, making the underside 525 mm above the floor.
Balanced materials: 25 mm birch plywood for the top and pine for the cleat. The top is cut to a true circle.

Legs are standard 21-inch tapered round table legs, approximately 40 mm at the top and 28 mm at the foot. Their centerlines splay 65 mm in both x and z over a 525 mm vertical rise, about 7 degrees in each vertical projection.
Leg ends are cut level with the floor and tabletop underside. Use suitable angled leg mounting plates or equivalent rated hardware; hardware is not represented as wood geometry.
The single 280 x 40 x 22 mm cleat is centered beneath the top as shown and fastened to the top. Legs attach independently to the top underside.

steps.title: Cut the tabletop and cleat
steps.text: Mark a 600 mm diameter circle on P1 (Round tabletop) and cut it with a jigsaw. Cut P3 (Underside cleat) to its specified 280 x 40 mm rounded-end shape; keep P2 (Splayed tapered round leg) uncut.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection and a dust mask. Clamp the sheet securely, keep hands clear of the blade, and support the offcut so it cannot pinch the blade.
steps.tip: Cut just outside the circle line, then sand to the line for a smoother, more accurate edge.

steps.title: Sand the parts
steps.text: Sand the cut edge of P1 and all faces and edges of P3, working through 120, 180, then 220 grit. Lightly sand P2 without changing its taper or level-cut ends. Remove dust before assembly.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection; collect sanding dust and keep it away from ignition sources.
steps.tip: Ease sharp plywood edges lightly, but do not round over the underside glue area for P3.

steps.title: Mark and drill the underside
steps.text: On the underside of P1, mark the centered position for P3 and the four leg-socket centers at the plan's 190/410 mm coordinates. Drill three clearance holes and 3 mm-deep counterbores through P3, clamp it in position, and drill three shallow pilot holes into P1. Use the certified gimbal-kit plate as a template and drill its four 6 mm through-holes at each leg location; do not drill or modify P2.
steps.safety: Clamp parts before drilling, wear eye protection, and keep the drill perpendicular to the top face when making through-holes.
steps.tip: Confirm the socket kit's template and documented compound angle before drilling. Check that each socket points outward toward its corresponding corner.

steps.title: Glue and fasten the underside cleat
steps.text: Spread a thin, even layer of wood glue on the mating face of P3 and align it with the marks on P1. Drive three Wood screws #8 x 40 mm through the counterbored holes from below into the pilot holes, spacing them evenly along the cleat. Clamp for 30 minutes, wipe away squeeze-out, and leave the joint unloaded for 24 hours.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while driving screws and keep hands away from the bit; wipe glue with a damp cloth before it cures.
steps.tip: Check the cleat is centered before driving the first screw; tighten only until snug so the plywood is not crushed.

steps.title: Install the certified leg sockets and legs
steps.text: Use one manufacturer-certified two-axis gimbal leg-socket kit at each marked location, following its instructions for 10° compound splay and plywood installation. Insert the kit's four M6 x 45 mm through-bolts from the tabletop top face, fit the supplied washers and locknuts below, and tighten them while the underside remains clear. Seat one unchanged, level-cut P2 leg in each gimballed socket and tighten the kit's two M6 socket-clamp bolts; this system has no hanger bolt and requires no M8 hole or insert in P2.
tools_used: Tools specified by the leg-socket kit
steps.safety: Support the tabletop securely while fitting the legs. Wear eye protection and keep fingers clear of the gimbal and socket-clamp pinch points.
steps.tip: Before assembly, verify the kit's documentation confirms the specified compound angle, level-cut leg fit, plywood compatibility, and lateral-load rating; a vertical-load rating alone is not sufficient.

steps.title: Apply the clear finish
steps.text: Apply three thin coats of clear water-based finish to P1, P2, and P3, following the product label. Allow about 2 hours between coats, lightly sand with 220 grit between coats if the label permits, and allow at least 48 hours after the final coat before careful use. Protect the floor and keep finish off exposed hardware.
steps.safety: Ventilate the area, wear gloves and eye protection, and follow the finish label; keep wet finish and used applicators away from children and pets.
steps.tip: Use thin coats and inspect the underside for drips before they dry.

steps.title: Inspect and test the table
steps.text: After the glue and finish have fully cured, set the table on a level floor and check for rocking, loose socket clamps, and loose through-bolts. Recheck the cleat screws and all four leg connections, then apply a gentle horizontal push to confirm the legs remain rigid. Use the table for ordinary side-table loads only; it is not a seat or step stool.
steps.safety: Keep the table on the floor during the stability check; do not climb, sit, or stand on it.
steps.tip: If it rocks, check the floor and that each leg is fully seated and clamped; do not trim the fixed legs to compensate.

plan.title: Classroom Desk and Chair Set
plan.summary: A single student desk with a matching chair, sized to resemble the classroom furniture in the photo. The dark wood-look desk top and red rounded chair panels capture the style; the frame is made from painted wood rather than welded steel tubing.
assumptions: The photo shows standard classroom furniture; with no target dimensions, the desk is estimated at 700 × 550 × 748 mm and the chair at 450 mm seat height and 800 mm overall height.
The plan is for one desk and one chair, arranged with the chair behind the desk; the chair seat begins 100 mm behind the desk's rear edge.
Balanced materials: birch plywood for the panels and top, poplar for the frames. Black paint approximates the photo's metal frames; red paint approximates the chair's molded seat and back.
The seat and back are flat plywood with rounded corners, not molded or curved. Rounded corners are described by a 35 mm radius.
The desk top is 18 mm birch plywood with a walnut-look HPL face. Wooden frame members are cut to actual dimensions and painted black.
Chair legs, rails, and back supports are glued and mechanically fastened at their touching faces. Desk aprons rest on the leg tops and support the desk top. Fasteners are not included in consumables.
