steps.title: Check stock and prepare the cuts
steps.text: Confirm each part matches the fixed dimensions and mark its identity before cutting. Cut the listed members from stock, keeping paired legs and rails identical in length. Use a straightedge to guide long cuts.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection. Support sheet goods securely and keep hands clear of the blade.
steps.tip: Label matching parts as pairs so desk and chair rails do not get mixed.

steps.title: Shape, sand, and predrill the parts
steps.text: Round the corners of P5 and P10 to the specified 35 mm radius, then sand edges smooth. Drill the pocket holes in P3, P4, P7, and P8, and pilot holes for the bracket and seat screws. Mark and drill the four M6 through-bolt holes in each P6/P9 splice, keeping the holes centered and clear of the ends.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection and a dust mask; clamp each part before cutting or drilling.
steps.tip: Test the 35 mm corner radius on scrap first. Use a drilling guide to keep the splice holes aligned through both mating members.

steps.title: Dry-fit and mark the frames
steps.text: Arrange the desk legs and aprons and check the frame is square before applying glue. Dry-fit the chair legs, rails, back supports, and splice plates, checking that the rear supports align with the rear legs. Mark the joint positions so every part returns to the same place during assembly.
steps.tip: Check that the chair frame sits flat on a level surface before fastening it.

steps.title: Mask glue areas and paint the parts
steps.text: Mask the wood-to-wood bearing faces and pilot holes so glue can bond to bare wood. Apply black paint to the frames and red paint to P5 and P10, following the paint label for coats and recoating. Allow at least 24 hours after the final coat before assembly, or longer if the label requires it.
steps.safety: Ventilate the area, wear gloves and eye protection, and follow the paint label for respirator and fire-safety requirements.
steps.tip: Do not paint glue faces; paint between assembled members can weaken the bond.

steps.title: Assemble desk front and rear aprons
steps.text: Glue the bearing faces where each P3 apron sits on P2 legs and clamp the frame square. Drive two 32 mm #8 pocket screws through the inside face of P3 into the side grain of each leg contact. Fit one 50 x 50 x 3 mm triangular steel corner brace inside each contact using its included screws; clamp for 30 minutes and allow 24 hours for glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep the driver aligned with the pocket hole to prevent cam-out.
steps.tip: Position each brace wholly inside the corner and check it does not obstruct the side apron joints.

steps.title: Attach desk side aprons and braces
steps.text: Glue the bearing faces where each P4 apron rests on its P2 legs and clamp the joints. Drive two 32 mm #8 pocket screws from each apron’s inside face into the leg side grain, then fasten one 50 x 50 x 3 mm triangular steel corner brace at each contact using its included screws. Check the base for square, clamp for 30 minutes, and allow 24 hours for glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep fingers away from the driver bit and clamping points.
steps.tip: Measure diagonally corner to corner; equal diagonals indicate a square base.

steps.title: Fasten the desk top with movement-friendly clips
steps.text: Install two figure-8 tabletop fasteners on each apron before setting P1 in place. Center P1 on the base, then drive the included screws into its underside from below. Do not glue the top; the pivoting clips allow seasonal movement.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and support P1 securely while positioning it; do not reach beneath an unsupported top.
steps.tip: Check the top overhang on all sides before tightening the final fasteners.

steps.title: Bolt chair back supports to rear legs
steps.text: Apply glue to the butt faces where each P9 support meets a P6 rear leg and align the pieces. Place one 200 x 20 x 3 mm steel splice plate on each opposite side of each joint. Install four M6 x 60 mm through-bolts per splice through the predrilled holes and plates, adding a washer and nyloc nut at each bolt; tighten securely, clamp for 30 minutes, and allow 24 hours for the glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and support the long pieces so they cannot roll or fall while fastening.
steps.tip: Keep each support and leg straight and flush at the splice; check alignment before tightening the bolts.

steps.title: Attach the chair front and rear rails
steps.text: Glue each P7 rail-to-leg bearing face and clamp the rail ends against P6. Drive two 32 mm #8 pocket screws at each listed contact, from the predrilled holes into the leg side grain. Check the frame for square, clamp for 30 minutes, and allow 24 hours for the glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep hands clear of the screw path.
steps.tip: Keep the lower rail edges aligned so the seat has even support.

steps.title: Attach the chair side rails
steps.text: Glue the P8 rail-to-leg bearing faces and clamp the side rails between P6 legs. Drive two 32 mm #8 pocket screws at each listed contact into the legs’ side grain. Recheck that the base sits flat, clamp for 30 minutes, and allow 24 hours for the glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep the frame steady while driving screws.
steps.tip: Check both diagonals before the glue sets so the chair frame does not rack.

steps.title: Brace the rear rail to the back support
steps.text: Glue the listed P7-to-P9 bearing face and clamp the members together. Install two 40 x 40 mm angle brackets at this contact using their included screws, driving into the accessible side faces. Keep the seat off until the brackets are secure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep the open chair frame stable while fastening.
steps.tip: Confirm the rear rail is level from side to side before tightening the brackets.

steps.title: Brace side rails to back supports
steps.text: Glue each listed P8-to-P9 bearing face and clamp it flush. Install two 40 x 40 mm angle brackets at each contact, using their included screws into the members’ side faces. Leave access to the inside faces for fitting the seat brackets.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and support the frame while drilling and driving screws.
steps.tip: Check that both back supports remain parallel before the glue sets.

steps.title: Secure the chair seat
steps.text: Apply glue to the rail tops and position P5, checking its overhang. Turn the frame upside down and support it securely; drive three 40 mm #8 screws through P7 and two 40 mm #8 screws through each P8 into the seat underside, using pilot holes and a depth stop. Fit two 40 x 40 mm angle brackets at each P5-to-P9 contact with their included screws; clamp for 30 minutes and allow 24 hours for glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and securely support the chair frame while working upside down; do not balance it on an unstable surface.
steps.tip: The 40 mm screws pass through the 30 mm rails and embed about 10 mm into the 15 mm seat; set the depth stop so they cannot pierce the top face.

steps.title: Attach the chair back panel
steps.text: Glue the P10-to-P9 bearing faces and hold the panel in its marked position. From the rear face of P10, drive three 30 mm #8 screws into each support, spacing them vertically and keeping the tips within the support. Clamp for 30 minutes and allow 24 hours for the glue to cure.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and support the panel so it cannot slip while you drive the screws.
steps.tip: Pilot holes help prevent splitting and keep the screw heads seated neatly in the panel.

steps.title: Touch up and allow the set to cure
steps.text: Touch up scratches and exposed edges with the matching paint, following its label for ventilation and drying time. Let all glue cure for at least 24 hours and paint cure fully before use. Check all screws, bolts, and brackets, confirm both pieces sit level, and do not use the chair as a step.
steps.safety: Ventilate the area during touch-up and keep the furniture out of use until paint is dry and glue has cured.
steps.tip: Recheck the chair after its first few uses and tighten any fasteners that have loosened.

safety_overview: Wear eye protection for cutting, sanding, drilling, and fastening; use hearing protection with powered saws and sanders.
Use a dust mask while cutting and sanding, and connect dust collection where available.
Clamp work securely, support plywood sheets, and keep hands clear of blade paths and screw paths.
Paint in a well-ventilated area; follow the product label for gloves, respirator use, flammability, and drying times.
This is movable classroom furniture, not wall-mounted furniture. Do not climb on the desk or chair, and keep the chair on a level floor.

review.summary: The desk frame and movement-friendly top attachment are generally workable, but the chair's back-support splice and small rail joints need stronger, clearer construction for repeated classroom use. There is also a mismatch between the rear-rail placement and its fit note.

issues.problem: The chair back supports are joined to the rear legs at a butt splice that must resist substantial leverage when someone leans back. The specified splice plates are only 20 mm wide on 30 mm stock, leaving little room for bolt edge distance and limited resistance to the joint loosening or splitting under repeated loads.
issues.fix: Prefer continuous rear legs that extend to the top of the back, eliminating this splice. If the splice must remain, use wider, appropriately rated steel plates and a documented bolt layout with adequate wood edge distances; verify the joint is suitable for repeated chair back loads.

issues.problem: The chair's front and rear rails are only 30 mm high and rely on two pocket screws plus glue at each leg contact. Together with the similarly small side rails in J9, these joints have limited stiffness against repeated side-to-side racking in a classroom chair.
issues.fix: Increase the rail section and use a stronger chair-appropriate rail-to-leg joint, such as housed or mortise-and-tenon joints, or add well-fitted structural corner blocks at the rail/leg joints. Apply the same reinforcement to J9.

issues.problem: The P7 rear rail placement specifies z=1055 and 25 mm depth, while its note says to adjust it to z=1050 and 30 mm depth for a flush fit. Step 11 then assumes the rail and back supports have a flush bearing contact.
issues.fix: Choose the intended rear-rail position and depth, update P7's placement and cut specification to match, and keep steps 9 and 11 consistent with that specification.

issues.problem: P1 is listed among the parts used in the painting step, but the step only describes painting the frames and the red chair panels. It does not say whether the HPL-topped desk surface or its edges need finishing.
issues.fix: State explicitly that the HPL face is left as supplied and specify whether the exposed plywood edges are sealed or finished; remove P1 from the parts used list if no finishing is intended.
